title: A third of the string
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: The shack's lights go up. A third of them work this year. Gully says last year was half. The uncle says the year before was a third. Gully says so it's going backward. The uncle says everything does, if you count long enough. Wood draws the dark bulbs as circles again.

panels.composition: The shack's eave. GULLY on the ladder with the string. The UNCLE in the chair below, the line. WOOD, BARNABY.

image.prompt: a stocky teenager on a ladder hanging a string of lights along a shack's eave while an old man in a lawn chair with an oxygen line watches from below, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The plug in. The string: lit, dark, dark, lit, dark, dark.

image.prompt: close on a string of holiday lights with two of every three bulbs dark, black and white, no words
a stocky teenager on a ladder looking at a string of lights, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The shack at dusk, a third lit. Wood drawing every bulb, the dark ones circles. Two-thirds circles. The strip counts what's out. It's learning to.

image.prompt: a shingle shack at dusk with a mostly dark string of lights along its eave, a young man drawing below, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen over rough blue pencil; xerox grain; stark spotting; rain in frantic vertical hatching (Arc 1's aesthetic)

notes: 'Everything does. Count long enough.' Two-thirds circles. (Dec 13 1999: half.)
